title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) to measure the marginal yield of applying a bounded deterministic generate–verify–repair (GVR) guard to a single shared LLM candidate per intent. Generation used gpt-5-mini and the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic, rule-based repair operator with repair_budget ≤ 1 (no extra LLM calls). Primary, artifact-backed outcomes are baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. The archived evidence bundle contains all prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts. We also report the confirmatory bank difficulty-label counts (easy=20, medium=80, hard=60, very_hard=40) and an auditable exemplar of the single repaired episode (task-000137) showing a MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND violation resolved by a deterministic Insertion transformation that changed validation_before.valid == false to validation_after.valid == true.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network-operations (NetOps) changes with large language models (LLMs) promises reduced manual effort but raises operational-safety concerns: LLM-produced configuration artifacts must be correct when applied to control planes. Prior intent-to-configuration prototypes demonstrate that LLMs can synthesize vendor-like CLI commands from natural-language intents but are prone to structured failures (missing commands, misordering, or protected-field modification). Proposed mitigations include retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool-augmentation. However, practical deployment settings often impose limits on hosted-model calls (cost, governance), motivating an estimand that isolates the effect of deterministic, auditable repair applied to the same initial LLM candidate.

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that shares a single initial LLM candidate across both arms (ungated baseline and guarded GVR). The shared-candidate estimand answers a concrete operational question: given one LLM output (cost-constrained regime), does a deterministic validator plus a single deterministic repair (when unambiguous) increase the proportion of emulator-executable configurations? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions and operational constraints of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; (3) exact-test justification and complementary bootstrap uncertainty quantification appropriate for small-discordant-pair inference; and (4) artifact-grounded clarifications requested during review: the aggregated per-task difficulty-label counts and an auditable exemplar of the single deterministic repair that changed an outcome.
sections.related_work: Existing literature intersects three strands relevant to this study. First, intent-to-configuration evaluations demonstrate LLM capability for producing CLI-like configuration artifacts but repeatedly document structural and semantic failures requiring post-processing; representative prototype and survey work summarize these findings and the diversity of failure modes encountered in NetOps contexts [doi:10.1002/nem.2313; OpenAlex W4411109869]. Second, mitigation strategies from NetOps and adjacent structured-generation domains include retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), live schema grounding, constrained decoding, and verifier-assisted repair; these reduce hallucination and format errors in tasks such as NL2SQL and document-grounded generation but require careful adaptation to vendor CLI dialects and workflow policies [doi:10.2139/ssrn.6909831; OpenAlex W4415680272]. Third, deterministic verifiers and emulator-backed validators provide an assurance layer: formal-methods tools (NetKAT variants, weighted NetKAT) and ensemble verifiers can check reachability and structural properties and are natural candidates for validators in NetOps pipelines [doi:10.1145/3808318; OpenAlex W7161165783]. These verification tools have known fidelity limits—control-plane dynamics and device-specific runtime behavior may not be fully captured—so emulator-grounded checks are necessary but not sufficient for production assurance. Our experiment situates itself at the intersection of these strands by measuring, under a constrained-call operational estimand, the marginal yield of a conservative deterministic GVR guard applied to the same initial LLM candidate.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration: The study followed a preregistered paired, shared-initial-generation protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). For each of n = 200 curated natural-language intents a hosted model produced one initial candidate configuration. That same initial candidate was (A) scored directly as the baseline and (B) deterministically validated and, if repairable and unambiguous, deterministically repaired for the guarded arm. The guard comprised a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic, rule-based repair operator invoked only when violation families belonged to a preregistered repairable set and a unique transformation could be determined. Operational constraints enforced by the preregistration were: maximum model-call budget = 400; repair_budget ≤ 1 deterministic repair attempt per episode in the confirmatory run; no additional LLM calls for repair. Realized provider accounting was model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared initial generations + 1 deterministic repair invocation implemented by code rather than a hosted-model call).

Task bank and scoring: The confirmatory bank contains 200 intent–expected-configuration pairs produced by a deterministic task generator. Each task payload encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (an authoritative ordered list of required commands), workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break, protected-interface constraints), and difficulty metadata. The scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) requires that generated configurations (a) parse syntactically into canonical CLI-like statements, (b) include the task’s required_sequence with correct presence and order, (c) respect dependency and group-activity policies, (d) preserve protected-interface values, and (e) produce, when applied in the deterministic emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR), a final_state equal to the expected_final_state. Provider/API generation failures are treated per the preregistered missingness plan as arm failures; none occurred.

Deterministic validator: The validator executes three ordered deterministic stages and emits a machine-readable trace used by scoring and repair logic. Stage 1 performs syntactic parsing and canonical normalization; syntax failures yield SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR and block deterministic repair. Stage 2 deterministically checks presence and ordering of required_sequence entries and enforces dependency/group policies; violation codes include MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, and TRANSIENT_ORDER_VIOLATION. Stage 3 applies the normalized configuration in the emulator and compares observed final_state to expected_final_state; validation_after.valid requires exact match. Validator traces record parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, violation_count/violation_codes, and validation_before/after summaries to support auditable failure-mode analysis.

Deterministic repair operator: Repairs are deterministic code transformations applied only when: (i) violation_count > 0 and the violation family is in a preregistered repairable set, (ii) a unique canonical transformation can be computed from the task payload (unambiguous mapping requirement), and (iii) the repair budget (≤1) is available. Implemented canonical transformations include insertion of missing required commands at canonical positions derived from required_sequence, stable reordering of annotated blocks to satisfy dependency rules, and deterministic enforcement to preserve protected fields. If multiple equally plausible repairs exist the operator abstains. All repair decisions and resulting normalized_configurations were recorded for audit. This design intentionally trades maximal-correction yield for auditable determinism and minimal hosted-call cost.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The confirmatory run completed all planned paired episodes (400 episodes = 200 intents) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level counts: baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). Paired contingency: n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact-test and interval estimates: The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test was computed using the two-sided binomial formulation on discordant pairs n = n10 + n01 = 1 with k = n10 = 1; the resulting two-sided p-value is p = 1.0. Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired-bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729), yielding a 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015]. Because the preregistered target absolute effect (0.15) lies well outside the observed CI, the confirmatory data do not support that magnitude of improvement under the shared-candidate estimand.

Repair and diagnostic accounting: The validator reported validation_before.valid == false in exactly one episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that single deterministic repair converted the episode into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). Syntactic/parse failures = 0 and provider-call timeouts/API errors = 0. Provider-call accounting records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1.

Aggregated difficulty-label summary (reviewer clarification): The confirmatory bank’s aggregated per-task difficulty-label counts are: easy = 20, medium = 80, hard = 60, very_hard = 40 (sum = 200). These labels reflect preregistered task-payload metadata used to span single-device and small multi-device changes; full per-task labels and payloads are archived.

Auditable exemplar of the single repaired episode (reviewer clarification): The sole repaired episode that produced the solitary guarded-only success corresponds to task_id task-000137 in the archived manifest. In that episode the validator emitted validation_before.violation_codes = ["MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND"] and violation_count = 1. The deterministic repair operator applied the canonical Insertion transformation (inserting the missing required command at the canonical position derived from required_sequence). After the deterministic insertion the validator observed validation_after.valid == true; the post-repair normalized configuration passed the full intent constraint checks. The episode’s repair decision and before/after normalized configurations are preserved in the archived run traces for audit.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and this curated confirmatory distribution the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic, auditable validators produce structured violation codes that enable targeted deterministic repairs; in this low-error regime the marginal yield of a conservative rule-based repair on the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by model-call budgets, the guarded shared-candidate design preserves low hosted-call cost while providing an assurance gate and a deterministic audit trail.

Statistical sensitivity and ceiling effects: The preregistered power/precision plan targeted an absolute effect of 0.15 with n=200 under conservative baseline assumptions. The observed baseline near-ceiling (0.995) dramatically reduced potential discordant pairs and thus inferential sensitivity for moderate sample sizes under the shared-candidate estimand. The exact McNemar (two-sided binomial on discordant pairs) is the appropriate small-sample test here; the chi-squared approximation is not appropriate for n small discordant counts. The paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] complements the exact test by bounding plausible paired differences and excludes large preregistered effects. Practically, designs that increase baseline variance (e.g., broader or intentionally harder task banks), change estimands (independent resampling: multiple independent LLM draws per intent), or permit LLM-invoked repair loops will increase power to detect non-negligible absolute improvements but at higher hosted-call cost and increased governance complexity.

Design trade-offs and practitioner guidance: The execution accounting (model_calls_used = 201; repair invocations = 1; completed_episodes = 400) supports explicit cost-versus-yield comparisons. Shared-candidate guarded designs are attractive when hosted-call budgets and tight auditability dominate. Conversely, independent-resampling or iterative LLM-invoked repair suits contexts where maximizing pass rates justifies additional calls. Deterministic validators are recommended as mandatory assurance machinery where auditable, repeatable checks and low-latency failure explanations are required. Importantly, the single repaired episode illustrates the practical advantage of deterministic repair in low-error regimes: a one-line canonical insertion converted a failing episode to a pass without further model interaction.

Failure-mode diagnostics and future work: Although confirmatory discordant-pair counts were low, validator traces capture rich per-episode diagnostics (violation codes, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, final_state diffs) that enable exploration of remaining failure-taxonomy questions in subsequent exploratory analyses. The preregistration anticipated that many remaining failures after deterministic repair might stem from emulator-modeled runtime or control-plane effects (e.g., convergence timing); those hypotheses remain unresolved here because only a single initial failure occurred in the confirmatory set. Evaluating broader repair strategies and multi-draw estimands remains an open operational question constrained by provider-call budgets and governance considerations.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is strong for the paired estimand and deterministic scoring; the experiment executed per preregistered protocol with complete accounting. Construct validity depends on emulator fidelity—our deterministic Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator models control-plane state deterministically but cannot fully capture runtime effects such as BGP convergence timing or vendor firmware idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by the single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic curated bank focused on small changes; extrapolation to multivendor CLI diversity or adversarial intents is limited. Conclusion validity is constrained by the near-ceiling baseline that reduced discordant-pair counts; the exact McNemar is appropriate but has limited sensitivity when discordant counts are small.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. For this estimand and task distribution deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded negligible marginal improvement, but deterministic validators remain valuable, auditable assurance gates for operational NetOps pipelines. The full archived evidence bundle contains the run traces and artifacts for independent audit and reanalysis.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: Generation requested gpt-5-mini. Validation used a deterministic netops validator implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by the study adapter. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤ 1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting: the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage invocations = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.
Full per-task difficulty labels and all run traces are archived in the study evidence bundle for audit and per-task inspection.
